title: White Screen of Death (WSOD)
description: Diagnose and fix a blank white page on the front end or wp-admin — usually PHP fatal errors, memory limits, or plugin conflicts.

steps.title: Enable WP_DEBUG and Check Error Logs
steps.instructions: Add WP_DEBUG, WP_DEBUG_LOG, and WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY (false on production) to wp-config.php. Check wp-content/debug.log and your host error log for the fatal error message.

steps.title: Use Recovery Mode or Health Check
steps.instructions: If WordPress emails a recovery link, use it to access admin with the faulty plugin paused. Alternatively install the Health Check plugin to enable troubleshooting mode.

steps.title: Deactivate All Plugins via FTP or Database
steps.instructions: Rename wp-content/plugins to plugins.off via SFTP, or set active_plugins to a:0:{} in wp_options. Reload the site — if it works, a plugin caused the WSOD.

steps.title: Switch to a Default Theme
steps.instructions: Rename the active theme folder under wp-content/themes. WordPress falls back to a default theme. If the site loads, the theme or its child theme is the culprit.

steps.title: Raise PHP Memory Limit
steps.instructions: Set WP_MEMORY_LIMIT and WP_MAX_MEMORY_LIMIT in wp-config.php (e.g. 256M). Confirm php.ini memory_limit with your host if errors persist.

steps.title: Reactivate Plugins One by One
steps.instructions: Restore the plugins folder name, then activate plugins individually until the white screen returns. Document the offending plugin and check for updates or replacements.

steps.title: Verify Front End and Admin
steps.instructions: Test homepage, key landing pages, wp-admin login, and any critical flows (forms, checkout). Disable WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY before closing the ticket.
